decisions.reason: A reference electrometer sits at the core of the firm's decades of dosimetry expertise, is a flagship shown on the home page, and is easy for the firm to interpret and improve.

Risk management software builds on the firm's QA software and integration capabilities and fits its move toward patient and machine QA convergence, giving it the related knowledge to refine the product.
A CT image quality phantom extends the firm's established imaging QA offer, so in-house R&D and physicist expertise allow it to learn from early market feedback.

Mammography phantoms lie further from the firm's dosimetry core, but its strong R&D, research cooperation and imaging QA line give enough absorptive capacity to assimilate this niche, so keeping it is likelier than dropping it.

The full field mammography phantom is distant from the core and partly overlaps Product D, which makes it a consolidation risk, but the firm's R&D base and expanding imaging portfolio favor retention for now.
The imaging QA instrument line is a flagship building on established measurement expertise and central to the firm's stated direction, so dropping it is very unlikely.
